legislation.cert_required: UL certification or equivalent safety standard
legislation.notes: Chapter 353 §7-321. A 'portable solar energy generating system' is LIMITED TO SUPPLYING A MAXIMUM POWER OUTPUT OF NOT MORE THAN 1,200 WATTS BACK TO THE ELECTRIC SYSTEM OF THE BUILDING - the building's system, not the grid. One system per electric meter, residential use only. The system is NOT eligible for inclusion in meeting the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard and MAY NOT GENERATE RENEWABLE ENERGY CREDITS OF ANY TYPE.
legislation.source_url_type: primary - Maryland Laws 2026 Chapter 353, chaptered text
legislation.effective_note: Emergency bill: effective upon enactment, 12 May 2026.

watt_tiers.basis: power output back to the electric system of the building
watt_tiers.effect: Not subject to §§ 7-306 and 7-306.1; the electric company may not require approval or charge a fee. One per meter, residential only. No RECs, does not count toward the RPS.

certification_requirement.quote: CERTIFIED BY UNDERWRITERS LABORATORY OR AN EQUIVALENT NATIONALLY RECOGNIZED TESTING LABORATORY
certification_requirement.note: Verbatim from the primary text. 'Nationally recognized testing laboratory' is the term used in 29 C.F.R. 1910.7; UL, CSA and Intertek/ETL are all NRTLs. A CE mark is a European self-declaration and is not an NRTL listing.
